notes:
Summary: Lumino Horizon is evaluating Redwood Dedicated + Private for mission-critical fraud detection and customer support. Primary drivers: predictable throughput for reranking/fraud scoring, low p95 latency for short-lived chat sessions, strict data residency and KMS integration. They are cost-conscious but willing to commit to reserved capacity if SLOs + SLAs are clear.

Workload & targets (quoted from CPO): "Need p95 < 120ms for scoring endpoint and sustained 150 req/s during market-open spikes; reserve capacity to handle 3x bursts for 30min windows." Also: reranking pipeline: p99 latency budget 250ms, throughput 400 qps daytime.

POC scope: validate throughput guarantees and autoscaling behavior. Redwood asked to prove: sustained throughput at target with cold-starts, scaling speed from 2->8 GPUs under burst, warm-pool effectiveness (pre-warmed model contexts), queueing/backpressure behavior under 3x load, and KV-cache performance with long-tail sessions.

Autoscaling & capacity notes: customer prefers hybrid approach: predictable reserved baseline (4-6 A100-equivalent GPUs) + ephemeral burst pool. Key asks: 
- scale-up policy: scale on queue length + CPU+GPU utilization, target add capacity within 30s for queued requests > 25.
- scale-down policy: keep warm-pool min 1 node per availability zone for 15 minutes after idle to avoid cold-start latency; aggressive scale-down only after sustained 10m idle.
- warm pools: pre-warm model shard and KV cache; test warm pool hit-rate and memory pressure during simulated traffic.
- queueing behavior: need graceful backpressure and SLA-aware priority for fraud scoring over support chat.

SLA / negotiation items: explicit latency SLOs (p95/p99), uptime 99.95% for dedicated baseline, credits for missed SLOs, outage runbook access, RCA timelines, support escalation path. They requested a pricing addendum for reserved GPU planning (monthly commitment tiers for 4, 8, 12 node baselines) and a scaling-cost calculator mapping bursts to overage rates.

Open questions / action items: 
- Redwood: provide detailed shaded perf curves (seq length vs tokens/sec) for recommended model variants and quantization profiles.
- Redwood: propose autoscaler policy templates and expected scale-up times from our runtime. Include warm-pool sizing recommendations.
- Lumino: produce network diagram for on-prem connector and confirm whether HSM/KMS will be customer-managed.
- Security: deliver SOC2 artifacts and encryption key lifecycle documentation.

Quotes and callouts: "We can accept some cold-starts for non-critical analytics, but fraud scoring must be near-instant — any burst must be covered by reserved baseline or immediate warm pool ramp." — Head of Fraud.

Immediate next steps: run 48h POC with traffic profile that includes: baseline steady load (150 rps), two 30min burst windows at 3x, long-tail sessions to exercise KV cache and rerank. Deliverables after POC: capacity plan with node counts for 99/95/90 percentile tolerance, SLA draft, pricing option sheet.
